title: Will and Verdict Anew
premise: When Odile Pemberton exhumes the coffin of Harrow's End founder Elias Verne for a land dispute and finds it empty, she uncovers a ledger of names hidden in the town archive—a century-old record of people who 'died' on paper but vanished alive, their identities traded to powerful families. As Odile follows the ledger's cipher, she realizes her own grandmother's name is in it, and that the town's founding dynasties have been harvesting inheritances from the erased ever since. The current heirs, led by Judge Ambrose Verne, will kill to keep the pattern running, and Odile—whose invisibility was itself engineered—must choose between exposing the town's rotten foundation or protecting the last living person listed: herself. In the end she publishes the ledger, convicts the judge with his own ancestor's forged death certificate, and reclaims her true name.
about_author: Astrid Crane is the pen name of a former records clerk who spent eleven years in municipal archives before turning to fiction, and whose fascination with paper trails outliving people informs every page. She writes from a coastal town not unlike Harrow's End, where she claims the cemetery is her favorite neighbor.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Odile Pemberton's POV. A routine exhumation order arrives for town founder Elias Verne, tied to a property lawsuit. Odile, who prides herself on knowing every grave, notes small oddities in the paperwork. Emotional beat: quiet pride and professional routine, shadowed by the first flicker of unease.

chapters.title: Empty Linings
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The coffin comes up clean, sealed since 1897—and empty except for a brass plate engraved with a number, not a name. The watching crowd of town elders goes still. Emotional beat: shock curdling into the realization that everyone present expected this except her.

chapters.title: A Town That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Odile investigates the burial records; every document is immaculate, too immaculate. Deputy Sorrel warns her, kindly, that some cases close themselves. Emotional beat: isolation—the first sense that her competence has made her dangerous.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: In the archive, Odile finds the town's founding donation ledger, its marginal numbers matching the brass plate. The entries are deaths that never happened. Emotional beat: exhilaration of the hunt, undercut by dread at what the pattern implies.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, flashback-tinged. Sorting her late grandmother's belongings, she finds a matching number sewn into a hem. Her grandmother's name appears in the ledger. Emotional beat: grief reframed as betrayal; the personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: Judge Verne Receives Her
chapters.summary: Ambrose Verne, patriarch and presiding judge, offers Odile a promotion and gentle warnings over brandy. He knows exactly what she's found. Emotional beat: velvet menace; power showing its polite face.

chapters.title: Nine Erasures
chapters.summary: Odile decodes more entries: nine people across a century declared dead, their assets absorbed by four founding families. She maps the beneficiaries. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the corruption isn't an anomaly, it's the architecture.

chapters.title: The Fire at the Archive
chapters.summary: Third-person limited via Deputy Sorrel. An overnight fire guts the records room; Odile's copied pages survive only because she broke protocol and took them home. Emotional beat: fear made physical; the enemy escalates.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Choice
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Torn between badge and conscience, he admits he was ordered to watch her. He gives her one name: the last erasure is scheduled—someone living, soon. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, guilt, the cost of complicity.

chapters.title: The Living Entry
chapters.summary: Odile traces the final ledger entry to a hospice patient, Ruth Okafor, whose identity paperwork was quietly rewritten last month. Emotional beat: urgency compressing into a race against administrative murder.

chapters.title: Paper Coffins
chapters.summary: Odile discovers how it works: a forged death certificate, a compliant coroner—her own predecessor's signature on every page. Her office was built for this. Emotional beat: horror of inheritance; she was hired to be the next instrument.

chapters.title: They Know My Number Too
chapters.summary: Odile finds her own childhood records altered—her name changed at seven, her history curated. Her invisibility was designed. Emotional beat: identity crisis; the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Verne House
chapters.summary: Odile breaks into the Verne estate seeking the original certificate book. She finds Elias Verne's real grave—dug deep beneath the family crypt—he died by his family's hand, the first erasure. Emotional beat: dread transmuted into righteous fury.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Bad Faith
chapters.summary: Verne confronts Odile with evidence of her own falsified identity, offering legitimacy in exchange for signing Ruth Okafor's certificate. Emotional beat: temptation and revulsion; the corrupt offer wears the mask of rescue.

chapters.title: Ruth Remembers
chapters.summary: Ruth Okafor's POV. The old woman reveals she was the ledger's keeper's daughter and memorized the cipher as a child. Emotional beat: fragile hope; two erased women recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Cipher Breaks
chapters.summary: Using Ruth's key, Odile cracks the full ledger: every founding fortune rests on stolen lives, including the judge's seat itself. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by scale—exposing this could burn the whole town down.

chapters.title: Silence Bought
chapters.summary: Sorrel disappears after refusing an order; Odile's office is sealed by judicial writ. Allies stripped away, she goes off the grid with Ruth. Emotional beat: darkest hour; the machinery closes around them.

chapters.title: What the Dead Would Say
chapters.summary: Odile stages a public viewing of Elias Verne's true remains in the crypt, forcing the town to witness its foundation. Emotional beat: defiance; turning secrecy into spectacle.

chapters.title: The Gavel Falls
chapters.summary: Climax. At an emergency hearing, Verne moves to have Odile committed; she produces the original certificate book and Ruth's sworn testimony, live-recorded. His own forged signature on his rival ancestor's death dooms him. Emotional beat: cathartic reversal—paper becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Arrests ripple through four families; Sorrel returns, reinstated. The town reels between shame and relief. Emotional beat: exhausted, unglamorous justice beginning its slow work.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Odile petitions to restore her birth name and visits her grandmother's corrected grave marker. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into reclamation; identity restored, not granted.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Odile's POV. Months later, she walks the cemetery renaming stones aloud, the ledger published as a memorial. A new case file lands on her desk—but this time nothing hides. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept, the invisible made visible.
